canonical_topic: Illiquid trading point / benchmark proxy risk
definition: The risk of approximating an illiquid physical trading location's price using a nearby liquid benchmark.
core_idea: Many physical energy trading points trade infrequently, so between actual trades there may be no fresh price available; the common workaround is to approximate the illiquid location's price off a nearby liquid benchmark, but the historical relationship between the two can break down without warning.
key_points: A trade's price is known at the moment it happens, but future prices depend on whether other participants trade at that same location
If a location doesn't trade regularly, a meaningful amount of time can pass before another real price is observed there
The standard workaround is to proxy illiquid locations off a nearby liquid benchmark
This proxy relationship is sometimes a reasonable assumption and sometimes fails when the expected relationship between the benchmark and the location breaks down
relationships: Related to parameter estimation risk as another consequence of limited market data
trading_implications: Positions or valuations at illiquid points carry basis risk to the benchmark used as a proxy
